newsitem.title: USA: Stocks hold gains after Fed keeps rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Stocks hold gains after Fed keeps rates unchanged.

text.p: Stocks maintained their strong gains on Tuesday as Wall Street toasted the Federal Reserve's decision to hold the line on interest rates.

Shortly after the central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee announced no change in monetary policy at 2:15 p.m. EDT (1815 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was up 71.77 points at 7,875.13. The index had soared more than 100 points in anticipation of the decision, but gains were eroded by profit-taking.
The announcement by the central bank left the key federal funds rate which banks charge each other for overnight loans steady at 5.5 percent, where it has been since March.
The next meeting of the FOMC is set for Sept. 30.

Economists had been nearly unanimous in their predictions that the central bank would keep short-term interest rates unchanged after producer prices fell in July for the seventh straight month and consumer prices inched higher.

The ideal inflation story propelled the stock market sharply higher this summer, although investors called a big time out last Friday to cash profits. That sell-off produced the second-largest loss for the Dow index since the 1987 market crash, sending the blue-chip index reeling by 247 points.

But buyers quickly returned to the market on Monday, lifting 109 points as investors shopped for bargains among well-known corporate names that had been battered, and they continued their buying spree on Tuesday.
